summary_paragraph: A male patient with end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis was admitted after developing transient substernal chest pain during a fistula thrombectomy procedure. Initial evaluation revealed elevated troponin and ischemic EKG changes, consistent with demand ischemia likely exacerbated by anemia from a concurrent GI bleed. He received one unit of packed red blood cells for a hemoglobin drop from 8.2 to 7.2 g/dL and was started on IV pantoprazole. Aspirin was given for cardiac protection, but heparin was avoided due to bleeding risk. His chest pain resolved without recurrence, and cardiac enzymes downtrended. Hyponatremia resolved with dialysis. A nonocclusive venous clot near the fistula was noted but not treated due to bleeding concerns. Digoxin was discontinued due to toxicity risk from elevated levels and renal failure, and cinacalcet was reduced for hypocalcemia. He remained stable, with no further bleeding or cardiac events, and was discharged home with follow-up plans.
problems: Atherosclerotic heart disease of native coronary artery without angina pectoris
Thrombosis due to vascular prosthetic devices, implants and grafts, initial encounter
Other forms of acute ischemic heart disease
